top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations A former FBI agent pleaded guilty Thursday to stealing about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency with wallet credentials the bureau had collected in its own cases, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia announced . Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, entered pleas to wire fraud and money laundering in federal court in Alexandria. U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea. He faces up to 20 years in prison and is scheduled for sentencing on March 4, 2027. Court papers put the illicit haul at $2,474,380.66. Prosecutors say Yaroch made roughly 100 fraudulent transfers using credentials tied to 35 separate FBI investigations, drawing on wallets controlled by investigation subjects, adversarial nation-state actors and at least one wallet the FBI itself had created for an operation. The Justice Department Office of the Inspector General had flagged the case in August after Yaroch’s arrest on a criminal complaint. That earlier account described a smaller set of transfers — about 10 moves totaling roughly $1 million — and noted that Yaroch self-reported the activity to two department employees on July 29, 2026. The plea figures are larger. From 2017 through early 2025, Yaroch worked in the FBI Boston Division on a squad focused on an adversarial nation-state. From February 2025 through July 31, 2026, he served in the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division at headquarters, with access to systems that stored cryptocurrency credentials gathered in investigations. How the FBI credentials turned into cash Beginning no later than December 2024, Yaroch used that access to move coins out of those wallets and into ones he controlled. After the transfers, he swapped the stolen cryptocurrency into other digital assets and ran further transactions meant to obscure its source, nature and ownership. Between Nov. 25, 2025, and Jan. 13, 2026, he moved about $93,082 into one of his accounts, then shuffled funds among other accounts to cover debts, including credit cards, car payments and loans, the office said. top.description: Credit: NBC Sports Bay Area The 2026-27 NBA season is underway, and while every NBA season brings plenty of change, it seems that some things are destined to always stay the same. The Golden State Warriors’ local NBC Sports broadcast team of Bob Fitzgerald and Kelenna Azubuike has finished in last place in Awful Announcing’s local NBA announcer rankings for three years running. Graders not only found Fitzgerald “condescending” and too focused on “teaching” the audience or complaining about referees, but the booth was also called out for its “homerism,” which even Warriors fans found excessive. That homerism reared its head again during Monday’s game between the Warriors and Phoenix Suns. Warriors forward Draymond Green was assessed a technical foul for throwing Suns center Khaman Maluach to the ground and escalating things with Suns guard Dillon Brooks afterward. However, if you let Fitzgerald and Azubuike tell it, everything Green did was within the lines. A notion so ridiculous that it wasn’t wasted on NBA content creator Kenny Beecham, who found himself on Awful Announcing’s 2026 list of rising stars in sports media. “I’m listening to this Warriors broadcast, and listen, they’ve been around for so long, this is not a new take, but I just remembered why the f*ck I don’t listen to the Warriors broadcast,” Beecham said on the Numbers On The Board podcast. top.title: Packers Insider Gives Team Clear Directive Before Trade Deadline
top.description: The Green Bay Packers and general manager Brian Gutekunst have been heavily involved in the NFL rumor mill leading up to the November 10 trade deadline. No one knows whether or not the team will make a big move, but the rumors have been out there that they have shown interest. Most notably, the Packers have been heavily connected to a potential blockbuster trade for Indianapolis Colts superstar running back Jonathan Taylor. They aren’t viewed as the front-runner to make that move, but they have at least had interest in swinging big. Over the years, Green Bay has not been known as an aggressive buyer at trade deadlines. Instead, the Packers have focused on drafting and developing, while adding veteran pieces around the edges. The trade Micah Parsons last year helped change some of that lack of aggressiveness. So far this season, the team has looked like a potential contender in some moments and a team who could miss the playoffs in others. They have the talent to be a Super Bowl caliber team. However, a move or two is needed. With that being said, one longtime Green Bay insider has spoken out with a clear directive for the team before the deadline. Indianapolis Colts running back Jonathan Taylor (28) takes off on a run Sunday, Oct. 18, 2026, during the game against the Tennessee Titans at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis. Green Bay Packers Urged to Get Aggressive at NFL Trade Deadline Sports Illustrated’s Bill Huber believes that it’s time for the Packers to make a Super Bowl move. He thinks they should be open to making a blockbuster trade. “To do big things requires bold actions. The Packers’ championship drought is too long. Now is the time to stop ‘being in every conversation’ and actually make the move to perhaps bring another title to Titletown,” Huber wrote . That statement from Huber is music to the ears of the fans. Green Bay has typically opted to not make the final move that could lead to a Super Bowl winning run. Making the trade for Taylor could be the final missing piece. The Packers could also consider an aggressive move to fix the offensive line like trading with the Philadelphia Eagles for Landon Dickerson. Only time will tell what Green Bay chooses to do. But, it’s clear that Huber and much of the Packers’ fan base believes that the time is now for Gutekunst and the front office to take a home run swing. top.title: ‘Social media made y’all way too comfortable’: Sophie Cunningham shares a message after election
top.description: Aug 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham (8) looks on during the second half at United Center. Mandatory Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images Sophie Cunningham had plenty to say on social media the day after the midterm elections. After sharing a post about “being better Americans” on Wednesday, the Indiana Fever guard followed it up with another message. This time, Cunningham shared a blunt quote from boxing legend Mike Tyson to her Instagram story, which took aim at people who feel comfortable disrespecting others online. Cunningham’s Post-Election Message On Wednesday, a day after Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, Cunningham reposted a lengthy message from podcaster and entrepreneur Andy Frisella to her Instagram story. The post argued that the country’s problems can’t be fixed through elections alone. “One of the strangest things about our culture is how much faith we’ve placed in elections to change our lives and how little faith we’ve placed in our own ability to do the same,” the post read. “Politics is downstream of culture. We can keep changing the people in charge, passing new laws and arguing over which party has the answers … but until we change the culture fostering, producing and tolerating the problems we have as a society, nothing fundamentally changes,” it continued. The post didn’t mention a party or candidate. But the timing was notable, coming from a player who has become a lightning rod for her political views. Cunningham sparked a firestorm this summer when she said she wants to protect girls from having to compete against “biological men,” comments that critics called transphobic. Still, Cunningham has insisted that her political views fall right in the middle . “I’m very much in the middle. I agree with things on both sides, disagree with things on both sides,” Cunningham told ESPN’s Hallie Grossman in July. Mike Tyson Quote Later, Cunningham shared another message to her Instagram story, this time a quote from Tyson. “Social media made y’all way too comfortable with disrespecting people and not getting punched in the face for it,” the post read, according to OutKick . Cunningham did not add any comment of her own, and it’s unclear what, if anything, prompted her to share it. She has been vocal about how she’s treated online, though. Earlier this week, Cunningham called her critics “ psychotic ” and said they have “so much hatred in their heart.” She also recently revealed that she has hired 24/7 security . top.title: Beach volleyball pro Alex Ukkelberg comes out: 'Thankful that I'm gay'
top.description: Alex Ukkelberg said he has been living his best life as an out gay man in Los Angeles for years, having come out to family, friends and in the pro beach volleyball community. But beyond that, it wasn’t until Wednesday that he said anything about it publicly. "There's no way I could be gay," the 32-year-old from tiny Battle Lake, Minnesota said in his coming out video . "Is there?" "When you grow up in a town of less than 800 people, being different is almost always a bad thing — and it’s definitely something you want to hide," Ukkelberg wrote in the caption. "I knew I was different from a young age.. but I didn’t know what that meant." “I’ve been out for a long time to family and friends and as I shared more on social media it just felt like a good thing to say. Visibility matters,” Ukkelberg told the LGBTQ+ sports site Outsports in an interview following his social media post. See on Instagram In his video, the former women's volleyball coach for the St. Cloud State Huskies talked about the various sports he played growing up: He ran track and competed in basketball, baseball, and football. Ukkelberg said while he knew he wanted to be an athlete, he said he thought that meant "there's no way I could be gay." That's the message he said the world reinforced, as he showed a flurry of images of him as both a student-athlete and as a guy dating women. Ukkelberg confessed that he actually didn't even think of himself as gay for many years. "Up until my sophomore year of college, I genuinely thought I was straight," he said, adding that he intensely felt the weight of finally admitting his identity for the first time. “Saying the words ‘I’m gay’ out loud for the first time was really hard for me,” said Ukkelberg. He added that he struggled with his sexuality so much that for a long time, he contemplated staying in the closet. But the toll of hiding who he was while pursuing sports was too much, he said. “After quite a few years of very bad mental health, I decided I wasn’t able to give up either identity. I was just going to have to figure out how to be both, and honestly, I’m thankful that I’m gay. It’s made me a better, more empathetic person,” said Ukkelberg. Tinubu made the remark on Friday during a reception and rally organised in his honour at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo. I love you with my heart. I will sleep in Akwa Ibom tonight. It’s going to be a second term presidential sleep. I will dream of victory too. “I will depend on you to go out and vote. Tinubu also reiterated his administration’s promises of improved living conditions, infrastructure development, education, skills acquisition and job creation. “I promised you a better future, I promised you development, I promised you education. I promised you skill development, I promised you jobs. We are going to plant a lot of economic trees,” he added. The President’s declaration comes amid criticism from the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, who had taken a swipe at him over his travels across the country. Obi had suggested that Tinubu had not spent the night in any state outside Abuja and Lagos, a remark that appeared to question the President’s physical presence across the country. Tinubu’s announcement that he would spend the night in Akwa Ibom comes against the backdrop of the exchange between the two political figures as political activities ahead of the 2027 general election gather momentum. nigeria.title: I’ll sleep in Akwa Ibom tonight – Tinubu

Tinubu made the remark on Friday during a reception and rally organised in his honour at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo. Addressing the crowd, the President thanked the people of Akwa Ibom for their support and urged eligible voters to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) ahead of the 2027 general election. “Thank you, Akwa Ibom. I love you with my heart. I will sleep in Akwa Ibom tonight. It’s going to be a second term presidential sleep. I will dream of victory too. “I will depend on you to go out and vote. The weapon you have is the PVC. If you have not collected it, please go ahead and collect your PVC. I am begging you, for the sake of your future,” he said. Tinubu also reiterated his administration’s promises of improved living conditions, infrastructure development, education, skills acquisition and job creation. “I promised you a better future, I promised you development, I promised you education. I promised you skill development, I promised you jobs. We are going to plant a lot of economic trees,” he added. nigeria.title: Lagos seals over 45 buildings in Eko, Ifako-Ijaiye
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Physical Planning Permit Authority (LASPPPA) has sealed more than 45 buildings in Eko and Ifako-Ijaiye districts over alleged violations of physical planning regulations. The enforcement exercises were carried out by the authority’s Monitoring and Compliance Unit on Wednesday in Ifako-Ijaiye District and Thursday in Eko District. In a statement shared on its Facebook page on Thursday, LASPPPA said 25 properties were sealed in Ifako-Ijaiye for operating without valid planning permits, excessive density, illegal remodelling, deviation from approved plans and ongoing construction without approval. In a separate update on Friday, the agency disclosed that more than 20 buildings were sealed in Eko District for various planning violations. It said 10 properties were found to have deviated from their approved building plans, while five were sealed for excessive density and another five for carrying out remodelling without the required permits. Other affected properties were sealed for undertaking construction work without planning approval. According to LASPPPA, the affected property owners and developers had earlier been served contravention notices by the respective district offices but failed to comply with the directives. “Contravention notices had been served by the district office previously, but compliance was not achieved,” the agency stated. The authority advised owners and developers of the affected properties to visit their nearest LASPPPA district office or its headquarters at Oba Akinjobi Way, GRA, Ikeja, for regularisation and further guidance. Meanwhile, a source in the agency, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said monitoring and enforcement of physical planning regulations were continuous exercises. nigeria.title: Kenyan preacher sentenced to 200 years in prison over child murders
nigeria.description: A self-proclaimed Kenyan preacher was sentenced to 200 years in prison on Friday for the murder of 190 children and one adult in an infamous starvation cult. Hundreds of bodies have been discovered since 2023 at the sect’s base near the coastal resort of Malindi, in what became known as the “Shakahola Forest Massacre”. Self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie, a former taxi driver, was accused of inciting his followers to starve themselves to death to “meet Jesus”. He was convicted last month of murdering 191 people between January 2021 and September 2023, alongside 28 co-accused. On Friday, the court sentenced him to 100 years for the homicide charges and 100 years for the starvation charges, while his accomplices — many of whom starved their own children to death — received a variety of lengthy prison terms. “Children observed siblings drop dead… as their parents ate and drank,” the judge said. “Some died as a result of strangulation, severely beaten… Children were subjected to extreme suffering… terrifying living conditions, psychological trauma.” Mackenzie was impassive as the sentence was read out, as he had been throughout the trial. Prosecutors had called for the death penalty, but the judge said it would “fail to achieve deterrence, particularly where the convicts regard death as a pathway to heaven and a union with Jesus and their deceased children.” Kenya has the death penalty but has not carried out an execution since 1987. Francis Wanje, a 62-year-old teacher who lost two grandchildren to the cult, told AFP he had hoped Mackenzie would be sentenced to death to prevent further tragedies. Another of his grandchildren, now 11, went without food for eight days before being rescued in March 2023. He testified that his brothers, aged two and five, had died after their parents, acting on the guru’s orders, forbade them from eating or drinking. “Nothing can ease the pain,” said Wanje, who blamed authorities for failing to act swiftly. “I really have great (anger) towards the authorities. If they had taken action, we would not be here today,” he added. – Death penalty – Mackenzie’s lawyer said he would appeal the verdict. He also faces manslaughter and terrorism charges in other trials, which he denies. Around 120 prosecution witnesses testified during the trial. According to witnesses, the movement denounced formal education as “satanic”, viewed modern medicine and hospitals as instruments of the devil and required followers to cut themselves off from the outside world. Mackenzie was arrested in April 2023 after a rights group alerted authorities and some followers were rescued from the 325-hectare (800-acre) ranch in the Shakahola forest on Kenya’s coast. nigeria.title: NDLEA remands two Mexicans, four Nigerians over Oyo meth lab
nigeria.description: By: Kingsley Omonobi The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has arraigned two Mexican nationals and four Nigerians over their alleged involvement in the establishment and operation of a clandestine methamphetamine laboratory in Tapa village, Ibarapa North Local Government Area of Oyo State. The six defendants were arraigned before Justice Nkeonye Evelyn Maha of the Federal High Court, Ibadan, on a four-count charge bordering on conspiracy, drug trafficking and the illegal production of methamphetamine. The NDLEA Director of Media and Advocacy, Femi Babafemi, disclosed this in a statement on Friday. The defendants are 56-year-old Mexican, Jose Villa Ochoa; another Mexican, Carrera Loaiza Arturo, 40; and four Nigerians identified as Maxwell Uche Nevoh, 30; Olatunji Yusuf, 37; Bankole Akeem Owolabi, 45; and Ganiu Monsiu, 43. According to the statement, NDLEA operatives arrested Ochoa and the four Nigerian defendants on June 17, 2026, in a forested area of Tapa village, while Arturo was arrested on August 19, 2026, at the Lagos airport while allegedly attempting to flee the country. Babafemi said the four-count charge accused the defendants of conspiring to operate a drug trafficking organisation and establishing a clandestine laboratory for the production of methamphetamine between December 2025 and June 2026 at different locations in Lagos and Oyo states. They were also accused of unlawfully transporting and distributing chemical substances intended for the manufacture of methamphetamine, contrary to Section 20(1)(f) and punishable under Section 20(2)(a) of the NDLEA Act. All six defendants pleaded not guilty when the charges were read to them. Following their pleas, Justice Maha ordered that they be remanded at the Correctional Centre in Ibadan. The case was adjourned until January 26, 27, 28 and 29, 2027, for trial. The NDLEA spokesman also disclosed that three other Mexican nationals and seven Nigerians arrested over a similar alleged operation at a forest hideout in Ogun State on May 16, 2026, had been remanded following their arraignment before a Federal High Court in Lagos. He said the court had rejected their bail application and ordered an accelerated hearing of the case. nigeria.title: FG targets 2,000 new CNG facilities nationwide
nigeria.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja The Federal Government has announced plans to deploy about 2,000 additional Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) infrastructure units across the country to accelerate adoption of the alternative fuel and reduce transportation costs. Executive Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (PI-CNG/EV), Ismaeel Ahmed, disclosed this on Friday shortly after the commissioning of a Rolling Energy CNG refuelling station for the State House in Karu, Abuja. Ahmed said Nigeria currently had about 160 operational CNG refuelling stations, while another 170 were at various stages of development or awaiting approval from the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA). He said the programme had moved beyond the proof-of-concept stage, with private investors committing about $2.6 billion to the development of CNG infrastructure. According to him, President Bola Tinubu has directed a fresh round of infrastructure expansion involving 1,500 units in February and another 500 in August through the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF). He said the additional facilities were expected to become operational between this year and early next year. “This is almost our 106th station across the country in less than two years. This is not beginning any longer. The market has been proven,” Ahmed said. He noted that Nigeria, with an estimated population of 220 million and about 12 million vehicles, needed to accelerate the deployment of refuelling facilities to meet growing demand. On the impact of CNG adoption on transportation costs, Ahmed said fares had dropped by between 30 and 40 per cent on routes where CNG-powered buses operate. He cited the Kano-Katsina route, where passengers who previously paid between N3,000 and N4,000 could now travel for about N1,500 using CNG-powered buses. “It has significantly reduced about 30 to 40 per cent of transportation fees in the routes where CNG buses are ferrying,” he said. The PI-CNG/EV chairman, however, acknowledged that existing facilities were inadequate to meet national demand, adding that the government was working to extend CNG-powered transportation to more commercial routes and underserved communities. Also speaking, the Permanent Secretary, State House, Temitope Peter Fashedemi, said the commissioning of the facility demonstrated the Federal Government’s commitment to leading by example in adopting CNG as an alternative to petrol. He said the initiative had become particularly important following the removal of petrol subsidy, which increased transportation costs and made cheaper alternative fuels imperative. Fashedemi explained that the State House partnered with Rolling Energy to rehabilitate an abandoned petrol station in Karu and convert it into a CNG refuelling and vehicle conversion facility. nigeria.title: Fani-Kayode disowns purported conferment of SCN rank
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s High Commissioner to South Africa, Ambassador Femi Fani-Kayode, has disassociated himself from the purported conferment of the Senior Counsel of Nigeria (SCN) rank, also known as Blue Silk, on him by the Nigerian Law Society (NLS). Fani-Kayode said he neither authorised nor personally approved the acceptance of the designation, describing the circumstances surrounding the conferment as an unfortunate administrative misjudgment. In a statement issued on Friday by his Special Assistant on Media, Lizzy Okoji, the former Minister of Aviation said his representation at the event by members of his staff followed an invitation sent to his office by the society as part of his official engagements. He, however, clarified that neither his staff’s attendance nor any communication subsequently made on his behalf should be interpreted as his personal endorsement or acceptance of the designation. The statement said the circumstances surrounding the representation and the subsequent communication of acceptance were regrettable and occurred without any intention to misrepresent his personal position or professional convictions. Fani-Kayode also raised concerns about the legal and professional implications of the purported conferment, particularly in relation to the statutory framework regulating the legal profession in Nigeria and relevant judicial pronouncements on the conferment of professional ranks outside the established legal framework. Describing himself as a legal practitioner of more than 41 years, he said he would not knowingly engage in any conduct that violates the law, undermines the integrity of the legal profession or brings it into disrepute. He added that he belonged to a family with three generations of legal practitioners and remained committed to upholding the law, professional ethics and the established traditions of the legal profession. The envoy said his clarification was intended to put his position on record, dispel misconceptions arising from the incident and reaffirm his commitment to the rule of law and the dignity of the legal profession. nigeria.description: By Sekinat Osundiji Nigeria’s representative at the Miss Globe 2026, Tracy Richards, has finished among the top 11 finalists at the international beauty pageant held in Phuket, Thailand. Richards also won the Head-to-Head Challenge and secured a place in the top 25 of the talent competition at the 23rd edition of the pageant, which concluded on Friday, November 6, 2026. Vietnam’s Nguyen Thu Thao emerged as the winner, while Thailand’s Suttida Iadpoo and Ukraine’s Mariia Zheliaskova finished as first and second runners-up, respectively. Richards hails from Ohaji/Egbema Local Government Area of Imo State. She is a high-fashion model and entrepreneur who co-owns a modelling agency. Beyond modelling, she is also involved in initiatives aimed at expanding opportunities for children in underserved communities through her advocacy project, Open Horizons. The initiative focuses on providing children in underserved communities in Lagos with access to mentorship, education and experiential learning through after-school programmes and educational outings. According to the project, the initiative is founded on the belief that exposing children to new experiences and opportunities can help shape their aspirations and future. Reacting to her performance, Richards’ team, in a post on Instagram on Friday, celebrated her top 11 finish and appreciated Nigerians who supported her throughout the competition. “From the moment she stepped onto the international stage in Phuket, Thailand, Tracy carried the Nigerian spirit, grace and determination with pride. What a journey, what a beautiful representation, and what an achievement to celebrate!” the team said. Thanking supporters who voted and encouraged the contestant, the team added, “To everyone who voted, supported, encouraged and stood behind her throughout this journey, THANK YOU.” It further described her performance as a source of national pride, saying, “Tracy, you made Nigeria proud. Your journey does not end here, and your light will continue to shine.” Her top 11 finish, victory in the Head-to-Head Challenge and placement among the top 25 in the talent competition marked a notable outing for Nigeria at the international pageant. nigeria.title: Four dead, 14 critically ill after suspected herbal poisoning in Benue
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi At least four persons have reportedly died, while 14 others are receiving treatment in hospital after consuming a suspected poisonous herbal mixture purchased in Oju township, headquarters of Oju Local Government Area of Benue State. The incident reportedly followed the sale of herbal preparations by three men identified as Alhaji Mai Magamani, Mohamed and Musa Kolo to residents of the Igede community during the Ihiejwo market day in Oju last weekend. An eyewitness said the incident came to light on Monday, November 2, 2026, after several residents who had purchased and consumed the herbal preparations began experiencing similar symptoms. According to the eyewitness, the first victim reportedly died on Tuesday morning, while the second died in the early hours of Wednesday. Two others subsequently died on November 4. The source added that more than 14 other persons were receiving treatment, with several reportedly in critical condition. The three men allegedly involved in selling the herbal preparations were reportedly apprehended by the Igede Youth Council in collaboration with the Oju Local Government Area Township Youth leadership and handed over to the police. The eyewitness said the Oju Divisional Police Headquarters had transferred the case to the Benue State Police Command for further investigation. Speaking during the handover of the suspects, President of the Igede Youth Council, Comrade John-Frank Ozzidi, called on the Benue State Government to ensure a thorough investigation and that anyone found culpable was brought to justice. Ozzidi said members of the community had resisted taking the law into their own hands, choosing instead to allow the police and other relevant authorities to handle the matter. He urged political officeholders from the area to monitor the investigation to ensure that the circumstances surrounding the deaths were established and justice served. Contacted, Chairman of Oju Local Government Council, Mr Jackson Ominyi, confirmed the incident but said he had yet to establish the exact number of fatalities. He said three deaths had been reported to him as of the previous day, while other affected persons were receiving treatment at the General Hospital, Oju. “My people are working on that. My security secretary, secretary and the security adviser are on it. “The others are in the General Hospital, Oju. My health department is also taking care of them. I have tried to calm the situation down. The person selling the herbs has been arrested and sent to Makurdi three days back,” he said. Efforts to reach the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Peter Aondongu, for comments were unsuccessful, as he did not respond to enquiries as of the time of filing this report. nigeria.title: Tinubu: We’ll turn stability into prosperity through enterprise
nigeria.description: President Bola Tinubu has said Nigeria’s next economic priority is to translate the gains of ongoing reforms into prosperity through enterprise, industrial growth and expanded trade. Tinubu spoke on Thursday at the opening of the 40th Lagos International Trade Fair, organised by the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), at Tafawa Balewa Square, Lagos. The President, represented by the Minister of State for Industry, Senator John Enoh, said the Federal Government had made significant progress in stabilising the economy, adding that attention must now shift to stimulating production, creating jobs and expanding business opportunities. “The emergency is over. The foundation has been repaired. Our task now is to turn stability into prosperity, and enterprise is at the heart of that task,” he said. Highlighting the administration’s economic achievements, Tinubu said Nigeria’s gross external reserves rose to approximately $55.07 billion in October 2026, the highest level in 18 years, while net reserves exceeded $40 billion, compared with less than $4 billion in 2023. He also noted that inflation declined to 14.63 per cent in September 2026, while the economy grew by 4.43 per cent in the second quarter, describing the figures as evidence of improving economic fundamentals. On trade, the President said non-oil exports exceeded $6.1 billion in 2025, while capital importation reached about $21 billion. He expressed optimism that Nigerian businesses could leverage the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) to access wider markets across the continent. However, he stressed that sustainable economic growth must be driven by domestic production and value addition rather than dependence on imports. Tinubu said the National Industrial Policy provided a roadmap for strengthening manufacturing, deepening local value chains and converting the country’s raw materials into finished products. He disclosed that the Federal Ministry of Industry, Trade and Investment and its agencies supported more than 115,000 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) in 2025. He assured business owners of continued government efforts to improve their access to finance, electricity and markets. The President described industrial and trade policies as complementary, explaining that while industry provides goods for export, trade creates markets for locally manufactured products. He also welcomed exhibitors from more than 20 countries to the fair, announcing that Nigeria would host the Intra-African Trade Fair for the first time in 2027, in partnership with the African Export-Import Bank (Afreximbank). nigeria.description: —Initiative promotes cheaper energy, attracts private investment — Perm Sec – –Says 10 JAC vehicles, Villa shuttle buses already CNG-hybrid By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA–The Federal Government has renewed its drive to promote the adoption of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) with the reopening of a former petrol filling station at the State House, Abuja, now converted into a CNG refuelling facility. Plans are also underway to extend vehicle conversion services to interested government personnel. The Permanent Secretary, State House, Temitope Fashedemi, stated that the initiative underscored the administration’s resolve to lead by example in promoting cost-effective and cleaner energy alternatives, while encouraging private-sector participation in the development of the country’s gas infrastructure. He explained that the Federal Government deliberately made the abandoned facility available for conversion to demonstrate the viability of the presidential initiative and encourage private investors to take advantage of emerging opportunities in the CNG market. He further explained the initiative is also aimed at addressing concerns over the limited availability of CNG refuelling stations, which has continued to constrain wider adoption of the alternative fuel. Fashedemi said government’s responsibility was to create an enabling environment for private-sector participation rather than take over the business of establishing and operating commercial refuelling facilities. He urged business operators and prospective investors to partner with Pi-CNG to establish more stations and vehicle conversion centres across the country. “All the filling stations you see around, are they owned by government? No. They are owned by people and business operators. The earlier existing and prospective business people recognise this as an opportunity and partner with Pi-CNG to establish these facilities, the better,” he said. The Permanent Secretary disclosed that the State House had already commenced the integration of CNG technology into its vehicle fleet, with about 10 recently acquired JAC vehicles being hybrid models, alongside some shuttle buses operating within the Presidential Villa. It was about the everyday struggle of ordinary people. It was about the mother working two jobs who still struggles to put food on the table,” Adesanya said while on Channels Television’s Sunrise Daily on Friday. “It was about the father who works 40 hours a week but still cannot afford to get decent housing. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Former FBI Agent Pleads Guilty to Stealing $2.47 Million in Crypto From Investigations A former FBI agent pleaded guilty Thursday to stealing about $2.47 million in cryptocurrency with wallet credentials the bureau had collected in its own cases, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia announced . Patrick Steven Yaroch, 37, of Ashburn, Virginia, entered pleas to wire fraud and money laundering in federal court in Alexandria. U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted the plea. He faces up to 20 years in prison and is scheduled for sentencing on March 4, 2027. Court papers put the illicit haul at $2,474,380.66. Prosecutors say Yaroch made roughly 100 fraudulent transfers using credentials tied to 35 separate FBI investigations, drawing on wallets controlled by investigation subjects, adversarial nation-state actors and at least one wallet the FBI itself had created for an operation. The Justice Department Office of the Inspector General had flagged the case in August after Yaroch’s arrest on a criminal complaint. That earlier account described a smaller set of transfers — about 10 moves totaling roughly $1 million — and noted that Yaroch self-reported the activity to two department employees on July 29, 2026. The plea figures are larger. From 2017 through early 2025, Yaroch worked in the FBI Boston Division on a squad focused on an adversarial nation-state. From February 2025 through July 31, 2026, he served in the FBI’s Counterintelligence and Espionage Division at headquarters, with access to systems that stored cryptocurrency credentials gathered in investigations. How the FBI credentials turned into cash Beginning no later than December 2024, Yaroch used that access to move coins out of those wallets and into ones he controlled. After the transfers, he swapped the stolen cryptocurrency into other digital assets and ran further transactions meant to obscure its source, nature and ownership. Between Nov. 25, 2025, and Jan. 13, 2026, he moved about $93,082 into one of his accounts, then shuffled funds among other accounts to cover debts, including credit cards, car payments and loans, the office said. FOX 5 DC , citing the same U.S. Attorney’s Office release , noted the Portugal planning that appears in the plea papers. Yaroch asked ChatGPT how to maximize investment returns and where to live in the European Union. He arranged travel to Portugal for September 2026. What the plea says the FBI lost The agreed statement of facts goes beyond the dollar figure. business.title: Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Rule to Allow Crypto in 401(k)s Arrives at White House for Final Review A final DOL rule that would ease alternative assets such as private equity, real estate and cryptocurrency into 401(k) retirement plans arrived at the White House on Thursday for review, Bloomberg Law reported , a procedural step that usually precedes public release. The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs logged the package on Nov. 5 under the title “Fiduciary Duties In Selecting Designated Investment Alternatives,” RIN 1210-AC38. The filing lists the DOL’s Employee Benefits Security Administration as the authoring office, marks the stage as a final rule, flags it as economically significant and notes that there is no legal deadline for completion. The DOL unveiled the proposal on March 30. In that draft, plan fiduciaries who follow a documented process when adding private assets to a 401(k) menu would get a legal safe harbor under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974. The six factors named in the proposal are performance, fees, liquidity, valuation, performance benchmarks and complexity. Satisfying them does not force plans to offer crypto. It lowers the litigation risk for employers that decide they want to. JUST IN: The White House is now reviewing a new rule which will allow Americans to invest in crypto through their 401(k) retirement plans pic.twitter.com/uXGGIXEzdC — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 6, 2026 What the DOL safe harbor covers President Donald Trump’s Aug. 7, 2025, executive order, “Democratizing Access to Alternative Assets for 401(k) Investors,” directed the Labor secretary to reexamine ERISA guidance and, where appropriate, propose rules with “appropriately calibrated safe harbors.” The order defined alternative assets to include private-market equity and debt, real estate, holdings in actively managed vehicles that invest in digital assets, commodities, infrastructure and lifetime-income strategies. The March proposal implements that order. A DOL fact sheet said prudence under ERISA is process-based and that fiduciaries retain discretion to select any designated investment alternative if they follow the outlined review. Deputy Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling cast the approach as neutral: “The department’s days of picking winners and losers are over.” That stance reverses a prior chill. In May 2025 the DOL rescinded its March 2022 compliance release that told fiduciaries to use “extreme care” before putting cryptocurrency on a 401(k) menu. The department said that phrase was not found in ERISA and restored a context-specific standard. Later, it was reported that Sens. Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren pressed the DOL to abandon the crypto-friendly path. House Republicans have separately pushed to codify Trump’s crypto order in statute. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Hackers Swap About $50 Million of Stolen XRP Mostly Into Bitcoin, Elliptic Says Hackers tied to the record Binance theft have begun converting a large slice of the stolen XRP into bitcoin, blockchain analytics firm Elliptic said in an update dated through Friday, with about 42 million XRP — roughly $50 million — already swapped, mostly through THORChain. Converted bitcoin from other stolen assets nearly doubled overnight to about 1,650 BTC, worth some $124 million, Elliptic wrote . Most of that jump came from the XRP route. About 192 million XRP, roughly $226 million, remained unswapped in addresses linked to the Binance theft. The XRP was part of the Oct. 29 drain that Binance later put at $6.34 billion. Between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC that day, five hot wallets sent 233.46 million XRP to an attacker address. The FBI has attributed the campaign to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it has frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion while covering customer losses from its own funds. How the XRP started moving The stolen XRP sat quiet at first. Early on Nov. 2, between 02:12 and 04:00 UTC, all about 233 million XRP moved into six new addresses, where it stayed until Nov. 5, Elliptic said . From the afternoon of Nov. 5, two of those six addresses began sending XRP on to dozens of new accounts that swapped it, mostly through THORChain into bitcoin. A small amount of ether also went through THORChain into bitcoin that evening. The main bitcoin and ether holdings from the theft — the largest pools — have still not moved, Elliptic said. That pattern matches what the firm saw after the Bybit hack: turn freezable and mid-liquidity tokens into bitcoin first, then attempt cash-out later through OTC brokers. The broader laundering trail is already vast. Since the Binance theft, Elliptic has counted more than 20,000 wallets on 16 blockchains, at least 36 services and at least 65,000 transactions — roughly one new wallet every 30 seconds and one transaction every 10 seconds. About $3.11 billion remains in addresses linked to the Binance theft, mostly as ether and bitcoin. A negligible amount has likely been cashed out so far. Why XRP and bitcoin matter here Issuers can freeze many stablecoins. They cannot freeze XRP the same way, and they cannot freeze bitcoin. After Tether and Circle locked down large stablecoin tranches on Oct. 29, the attacker prioritized assets that sit outside that kill switch. Swapping XRP into bitcoin continues that logic: bitcoin is harder to claw back once it is fragmented across fresh addresses. All of the stolen SOL, about $87 million at Elliptic’s prices, has already been swapped, bridged or mixed, with much of it ending as bitcoin. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Holds Near $75,000 After Hot October Jobs Report U.S. employers added 165,000 jobs in October, nearly three times the 59,000 economists expected, the Labor Department said Friday, and the bitcoin price briefly pushed above $76,100 before settling near $75,500, Bitcoin Magazine Pro data shows. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1% from 4.2%, beating the Dow Jones forecast that called for it to hold. Average hourly earnings rose 0.4% on the month and 3.1% over the year, both ahead of estimates, CNBC reported . Prior months were revised higher as well. August payrolls moved to 186,000, an upward revision of 53,000, and September rose to 60,000 after a 31,000 upgrade, leaving the two-month total 84,000 stronger than first reported. The print lands on a market still digesting Thursday’s Nasdaq-led rout. The bitcoin price had held near $76,000 into that close, dipped toward $75,200 late in the session, then recovered into the mid-$75,000s overnight before the 8:30 a.m. ET release. Spot bitcoin changed hands around $75,800 after the data, with a market cap of about $1.52 trillion and roughly $48 billion in trading volume over the past day, Yahoo Finance data indicated. Bitcoin price reaction Bitcoin price’s first move was a quick spike above $76,100, then a slide toward $75,600 before it settled back near $75,800. The range on the day has run from about $75,240 to $76,280, leaving the market little changed from its pre-release level even as rate futures repriced. That muted finish fits the pattern after big macro prints. Most of the damage to the bitcoin price this week came from equity risk-off, not from the labor market itself, and a hot payrolls number mainly reinforces the path the Fed was already pricing. CME FedWatch odds put roughly a 79% chance of a 25-basis-point hike at the Dec. 9 meeting after the release, up from about 70% into the open. The next employment report is due Dec. 4, five days before that decision, and the signal points the same way the last Fed hold did: stronger hiring and firmer wages leave less room for another pause. The Nasdaq Composite fell about 5.5% and dropped into correction territory, more than 10% below its recent high, while the S&P 500 lost about 4.4% and the Dow shed roughly 1,800 points, or 3.4%, CNBC reported . The Magnificent Seven erased more than $1 trillion in market value. Nvidia alone lost more than 9%, wiping out roughly $440 billion in capitalization, as investors priced in a slower AI data-center buildout after the Democratic midterm sweep. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korean Crypto Exchange Gopax Suspends Withdrawals and Trading After Hacking Threat South Korean cryptocurrency exchange Gopax suspended withdrawals and trading on Friday after receiving a hacking-threat email, and said it is moving all held virtual assets into offline cold wallets as a preemptive step to protect customer funds. Gopax halted standard deposit and withdrawal services at 2:55 p.m. local time and stopped trading at 3:53 p.m., Yonhap News Agency reported , citing the exchange. Direct withdrawals through the website and app are unavailable. Customers who want coins out must apply through the customer support center, where requests are processed manually after internal verification. “To ensure the safe custody of user assets, we plan to transfer all virtual assets to cold wallets for storage,” Gopax said in remarks carried by Seoul Economic Daily. “Direct withdrawals through the Gopax website or app are temporarily unavailable, and customers wishing to withdraw funds should apply through the Gopax customer support center.” No actual loss of assets has been reported. The company has not set a date to reopen trading or standard withdrawals. What Gopax closed and what still works With trading offline, all open orders were canceled, Chosun Biz reported . Deposits were initially paused with withdrawals; later Korean coverage said deposits had been restored while web and app withdrawals stayed shut. Manual withdrawals through support will take longer than usual. A cold wallet is a storage setup kept offline, cut off from the internet that hot wallets use to process customer sends. Gopax said the shift of remaining hot-wallet balances into cold storage is meant to shrink the surface available to anyone who can reach online systems. A Gopax official told Yonhap the email came from a party claiming it could hack the exchange, but that the threat itself had not been verified. “We ask for your understanding, as this measure is intended to prevent financial incidents and protect user assets,” the company said . A rough stretch for Korean crypto platforms The freeze lands in a week when exchange security is already under a bright light. On Oct. 29, attackers drained about $6.34 billion from Binance hot wallets in what Binance later described as a months-long campaign that began with a fake job interview. The FBI has tied that theft to North Korea; Binance has reopened withdrawals in stages and said it is covering customer losses from its own funds. Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin froze deposits and withdrawals earlier this week after its own security incident, with preliminary estimates of suspicious transfers near $40 million. Gopax’s case is different on the facts disclosed so far: the exchange is describing a threat email and a precautionary lockdown, not a confirmed drain. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Argentine Bitcoiners Debut “The Genesis of Satoshi Nakamoto” Artwork in Downtown Buenos Aires “The Genesis of Satoshi Nakamoto,” a 2.4-meter, multi-dimensional cube, was presented on October 29 at Polo Dot as part of the Open Fest of LABITCONF 2026 . Driven by Bitcoin.ar through the Premio B·Arte, the work combines art, technology, and education in a journey through Bitcoin’s fundamental principles. The inauguration featured guided remarks by Rodolfo Andragnes and a musical performance by Mayumaná, according to an announcement by the organization. Buenos Aires now has a monument dedicated to Satoshi Nakamoto, the person—or group of people—behind the creation of Bitcoin, whose identity remains unknown. Driven by Bitcoin.ar through the fifth edition of the Premio B·Arte, the monument was conceived not only as a tribute to Satoshi, but also as an artistic and educational experience. Through its five faces—four lateral and one upper—it proposes a journey to approach different concepts that explain Bitcoin’s origin, functioning, and philosophy. During the inauguration, Rodolfo Andragnes — co-founder of Bitcoin.ar and LABITCONF — accompanied the public with words and explanations about the details of the work, guiding the reading of its various elements and the meaning behind each representation. The presentation was accompanied by a musical show by Mayumaná, which added rhythm and sound to the opening of this new space dedicated to Bitcoin’s history. Five faces to discover Bitcoin’s history and principles Each of the monument’s faces offers a gateway to a different aspect of Bitcoin. The figure of Satoshi Nakamoto, for example, represents the anonymous character of its creator and the collective dimension of a technology that, once set in motion, continued to grow thanks to thousands of people distributed around the world. The reflections and multiplied geometric forms also evoke the structure of a network that replicates and expands. Another of its faces addresses Bitcoin’s programmed scarcity through a cube that successively divides into halves in a Fibonacci sequence. The representation refers to “the halving”, the mechanism that approximately every four years halves the reward miners receive for validating blocks and that regulates the issuance of new bitcoins. Starting at 50 bitcoins per block, the total reward gets cut in half every four years for roughly 130 years, until 21 million bitcoins have been emitted and the block reward becomes zero. This supply limit is iconic to the cryptocurrency and key to its qualities as hard money. The work also incorporates the first words of Bitcoin’s foundational document, the white paper published by Satoshi Nakamoto in October 31st, 2008. There, the possibility of making electronic payments directly between people, without needing to go through a financial institution, is proposed. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. entertainment.description: OBIMI CIC is a UK-based community organisation supporting parents and caregivers of children with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). Its founder, Helen Ewumi , is a qualified social worker and a parent of children with disabilities. Her professional experience and family life both inform OBIMI’s commitment to helping families feel heard, supported and less alone. The Nigeria outreach brought families together in Lagos to share experiences and raise awareness about the importance of understanding disability and challenging stigma. Around 100 families received support through the outreach, including food hampers. Clothing was also shared with families. During the visit, the OBIMI team went to a special school in Lagos and gave pupils school bags and stationery. These practical gifts were offered to support children with their learning and to remind them that they are valued and included. The gathering also created space for families to connect and take part in conversations about disability. OBIMI’s message was clear: every child deserves to belong, and families should be met with understanding, respect and support. For Helen, taking OBIMI’s work to Nigeria was an opportunity to connect with families and communities in Lagos. As a social worker and a parent with lived experience of caring for children with disabilities, she understands how important it is for families to feel listened to and supported. OBIMI CIC is grateful to the families, school staff, volunteers, partners and supporters who helped make the outreach possible. The organisation hopes to continue building connections and raising awareness so that children with disabilities and their families can feel seen, supported and included. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Loving Itohan is in cinemas nationwide from 6 November 2026. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.description: Credit: NBC Sports Bay Area The 2026-27 NBA season is underway, and while every NBA season brings plenty of change, it seems that some things are destined to always stay the same. The Golden State Warriors’ local NBC Sports broadcast team of Bob Fitzgerald and Kelenna Azubuike has finished in last place in Awful Announcing’s local NBA announcer rankings for three years running. Graders not only found Fitzgerald “condescending” and too focused on “teaching” the audience or complaining about referees, but the booth was also called out for its “homerism,” which even Warriors fans found excessive. Mandatory Credit: Kamil Krzaczynski-Imagn Images Sophie Cunningham had plenty to say on social media the day after the midterm elections. After sharing a post about “being better Americans” on Wednesday, the Indiana Fever guard followed it up with another message. This time, Cunningham shared a blunt quote from boxing legend Mike Tyson to her Instagram story, which took aim at people who feel comfortable disrespecting others online. Cunningham’s Post-Election Message On Wednesday, a day after Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, Cunningham reposted a lengthy message from podcaster and entrepreneur Andy Frisella to her Instagram story. The post argued that the country’s problems can’t be fixed through elections alone. “One of the strangest things about our culture is how much faith we’ve placed in elections to change our lives and how little faith we’ve placed in our own ability to do the same,” the post read. “Politics is downstream of culture. The post didn’t mention a party or candidate. But the timing was notable, coming from a player who has become a lightning rod for her political views. Cunningham sparked a firestorm this summer when she said she wants to protect girls from having to compete against “biological men,” comments that critics called transphobic. Still, Cunningham has insisted that her political views fall right in the middle . “I’m very much in the middle. I agree with things on both sides, disagree with things on both sides,” Cunningham told ESPN’s Hallie Grossman in July. Cunningham did not add any comment of her own, and it’s unclear what, if anything, prompted her to share it. She has been vocal about how she’s treated online, though. Earlier this week, Cunningham called her critics “ psychotic ” and said they have “so much hatred in their heart.” She also recently revealed that she has hired 24/7 security . sports.title: Beach volleyball pro Alex Ukkelberg comes out: 'Thankful that I'm gay'
sports.description: Alex Ukkelberg said he has been living his best life as an out gay man in Los Angeles for years, having come out to family, friends and in the pro beach volleyball community. But beyond that, it wasn’t until Wednesday that he said anything about it publicly. "There's no way I could be gay," the 32-year-old from tiny Battle Lake, Minnesota said in his coming out video . "Is there?" "When you grow up in a town of less than 800 people, being different is almost always a bad thing — and it’s definitely something you want to hide," Ukkelberg wrote in the caption. "I knew I was different from a young age.. but I didn’t know what that meant." “I’ve been out for a long time to family and friends and as I shared more on social media it just felt like a good thing to say. Visibility matters,” Ukkelberg told the LGBTQ+ sports site Outsports in an interview following his social media post. See on Instagram In his video, the former women's volleyball coach for the St. Cloud State Huskies talked about the various sports he played growing up: He ran track and competed in basketball, baseball, and football. Ukkelberg said while he knew he wanted to be an athlete, he said he thought that meant "there's no way I could be gay." That's the message he said the world reinforced, as he showed a flurry of images of him as both a student-athlete and as a guy dating women. Ukkelberg confessed that he actually didn't even think of himself as gay for many years. "Up until my sophomore year of college, I genuinely thought I was straight," he said, adding that he intensely felt the weight of finally admitting his identity for the first time. “Saying the words ‘I’m gay’ out loud for the first time was really hard for me,” said Ukkelberg. sports.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images While the Atlanta Falcons are fighting for their season, the 24-year-old running back is actively planning his life after the gridiron. He told the New York Post that he is taking serious steps to launch an acting career. He even wants to star in a romantic comedy. This is more than a hobby for a rich athlete. He is enrolling in acting classes to learn the craft from the ground up. He appeared as himself on the Disney Channel show “Bunk’d: Learning The Ropes” last July. He also made a cameo in the Netflix series “Outerbanks” in October. Those roles were fun, but he wants more. He said he is ready to move past commercials and into serious drama. “I’m willing to kind of explore anything more on the drama side,” Robinson said on behalf of Invisalign. A Plan for Life After Football The 2026 season has been tough for the Falcons. They sit at 3-5 after a 16-0 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday. Robinson knows the team needs him to be better. He has 780 rushing yards and four touchdowns so far. Yet he refuses to accept praise as the league’s top back. “I’ll be honest, like, I don’t feel like I’m playing like that right now,” Robinson said, in comments shared by Falcons reporter Daniel Flick. He demands more from himself for the offense to succeed. He launched his own DJ series called “Spin Zone” in September 2024. He sees these projects as a way to grow as a person. “I want to continue to put myself in different brackets of life,” Robinson said. He plans to dig deep into acting classes at the end of the year. He wants to gain the talent and charisma needed to succeed on screen, not just because he is an NFL star. Advice for Struggling Stars Robinson uses his own experiences to help others facing pressure. He is in Madrid this week to play the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday, November 8. He plans to meet with Real Madrid soccer stars Vinícius Júnior and Kylian Mbappé before the game. Vinícius is going through a slump and dealing with a four-game suspension. Robinson offered simple advice to help the Brazilian player. “I’ll tell (Vinícius), just stay the course. Don’t worry about external noise,” Robinson said. He warned that listening to critics can hurt a player’s mind. He knows what it feels like to have bad weeks. He told Vinícius to trust that God’s plan for his career would be amazing. “If you have an up-and-down or a low or something like that, we all have those moments and we all had those weeks,” Robinson said. The running back wears number 7, just like Vinícius. They met through a jeweler a few years ago.

sports.title: Oscar Piastri pays tribute to Australian F1 legend Alan Jones following his death
sports.description: Motorsport photo McLaren's Oscar Piastri has paid tribute to Alan Jones following the death of Australia's 1980 Formula 1 world champion. Jones died at the age of 80 on 5 November 2026, following a short illness. He won 12 grands prix, celebrated 24 podium finishes and gave Williams its first drivers' title. He also remains the last Australian to have won the Australian Grand Prix at Calder Park in 1980. Jones competed in the championship from 1975 to 1981, in 1983 and again from 1985 to 1986. In addition to Williams, he also drove for Hesketh, Hill, Surtees, Shadow, Arrows and Haas-Lola. Speaking to F1.com at Interlagos ahead of the Brazilian Grand Prix weekend, Piastri said: "It's obviously a very sad day. A life that should be very well celebrated. I think [he was] a guy who obviously had a lot of success on the racetrack and was Australia’s most recent world champion. "But I think also the person he was, you know, a very straightforward person, straight to the point. On a personal level as well, he often had nice things to say about me, which was nice." Frank Dernie, Frank Williams and Alan Jones Frank Dernie, Frank Williams and Alan Jones The Australian driver revealed he had driven the Williams in which Jones won his title. "I’ve had the honour to drive his world championship-winning car as well, so [it was] very cool to be able to experience that and connect with him in some kind of way. A sad day, but a day that should celebrate a great life. "Obviously, he was a long, long time before me, and I never had much interaction with Alan. But I think in a lot of ways, he kind of embodied the Australian spirit – very tough, saying it how it is, saying what he thinks, and I think that’s probably the biggest thing. "Anyone who’s won a world championship in F1 has clearly achieved it through talent, hard work, all kinds of other things, so I think that probably says enough." sports.description: Taylor Swift was there at the New York Knicks' magical Game 4 to see the 29-point comeback last spring and the OG Anunoby tip-in , and while there were a lot of questions about whether or not she's a Knicks fan , she is. Both Kolek and Swift share Rhode Island connections. Kolek is from Cumberland and was a standout player at both Cumberland High and St. George's School. He played college ball at both George Mason and then Marquette, where he won Big East Player of the Year honors in 2022-23. He was drafted 34th overall in the 2024 NBA Draft by the Portland Trail Blazers but was traded to the New York Knicks on draft night. Swift, of course, is one of the most famous and successful singers on the planet. She is a 14-time Grammy Award winner and has compiled hundreds of other awards. In 2013, she bought a mansion in Watch Hill, formerly known as the “Holiday House," complete with an Olympic-sized swimming pool, a bedroom suite, and a past that ties it to the Standard Oil fortune. Swift married NFL star Travis Kelce on July 3 in a star-studded event at Madison Square Garden, after rumors swirled last year that the wedding could take place in Westerly. technology.description: The US Department of Justice (DoJ) says its Super Intelligence Task Force (SINTF) is now up and running, after president Donald Trump ordered the move in a memo last month. Headed up by director of national intelligence Jay Clayton, as well as associate attorney general Stanley Woodward and associate deputy attorney general Stephen Weiss, SINTF's responsibility is to protect the US's lead in artificial intelligence development. Thursday's announcement, which was littered with the " super intelligence " Trumpism, said the task force will ensure the US's SI/AI leadership remains uncompromised by foreign AI "abuse," including by state and state-backed groups, criminal enterprises, individuals, or corporate entities. Per Trump's October 13 memo [PDF], SITF will take "affirmative measures, as appropriate," to ensure the US stays ahead in AI development. It did not elaborate on what this nebulous phrase meant, but it can be reasonably assumed this means a breadth of proactive steps. The memo also stated that the task force will organize the DoJ's criminal and civil lawsuits involving AI, recommend enforcement priorities concerning public safety and AI misuse, develop prosecution guidance for unlawful AI conduct, and feed into legislative proposals to prevent "burdensome regulation." Addressing a Wall Street Journal tech conference this week, Pentagon CTO and SITF vice chair Emil Michael said the team would release details about its AI regulatory landscape later this month. The task force will also shoulder various cross-departmental responsibilities, such as "deconflicting investigations, cases, and other matters" among departments and the offices of US attorneys. According to quotes from senior officials, chief among the concerns facing ordinary US citizens are AI attacks that target individuals, as well as those that aim to disrupt critical infrastructure and other national security interests. "The creation of the DOJ-SITF marks an important moment for the Department to help advance SI technologies and, at the same time, protect American innovation," said Weiss. "The Department also has a responsibility to utilize law enforcement tools at our disposal to deter improper use of SI, harden regular reporting on SI risk and response, and ensure companies exercise vigorous internal controls so that SI technology behaves as intended. The Department is committed to protecting all Americans and our business interests." technology.title: Crowd fave Linux Mint update approaches, fresh from autumn release of Cinnamon desktop
technology.description: Linux Mint 27 is expected next month, and it's starting to take shape. Its flagship desktop, Cinnamon 2.8, is already available. The team behind the popular, beginner-friendly Linux just released Cinnamon 2.8 , which will be the default desktop in Mint 27. Since 2014, Linux Mint versions have been based on the LTS releases of Ubuntu. Since a new LTS, Ubuntu 26.04 "Resolute Raccoon" arrived in late April , that means that a corresponding version of Mint is in development. The Mint project blog post last month revealed the codename: "Adrien." This is the first male codename since Mint 1.0 "Ada" in 2006, based on the first ever Ubuntu LTS release, 6.06 "Dapper Drake", but the project has run through the whole alphabet since then (except for the letter “Y”.) That blog also revealed it will have a new alarm clock app, but the subsequent Mint Blog post imparted more information. The Nemo file manager will gain a preview pane, there will be a new and much more capable system resource-monitor program called "Superlight", a new simple manager for compressed archive files (Zip and so on) called "Unfold," and a new, theme-able terminal emulator called "Velocitty." Mint also has a new Community Website , which uses GitHub to manage logins and eliminates the old website's dependency on PHP. Probably the most significant new feature, though, is that Mint 27 will restore system hibernation. Ubuntu supported hibernation in its early releases, but it has been disabled as standard since 12.04 "Precise Pangolin." Enabling it again is regularly discussed, for instance back in 2020 . As we discussed in some detail a year ago , it's a complicated subject and there's a lot that can go wrong. It seems that Mint's Clément Lefebvre feels he can sort this, and we hope it works out. Support is included in the new version of Cinnamon, among a host of other changes. Its Wayland support is no longer experimental, although the X11 session is still there so users won't be forced to use the new system. The Network Manager applet has better, simpler VPN support and Wi-Fi encryption handling. There are multiple improvements across the desktop: better handling of sound devices, keyboard input layouts, touchpads and gesture support, HiDPI display handling, and better search in the Settings app. The window list control has been upgraded, more things happen in the background for faster desktop starts, and it has better handling and storage of authentication and credentials, including the same Rust-based "oo7" secret store we mentioned in Fedora 45 . Screensaver handling is also mentioned – this is particularly problematic under Wayland, as XScreensaver maintainer Jamie Zawinski has covered with some feeling . The Mint blog mentioned this at the start of 2026 , when Lefebvre announced the new, slower, annual release schedule.
